data.title: Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
data.description: HONG KONG, Nov 24 : Asian shares leapt on Tuesday following a spectacular Wall Street surge as Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO sparked a relief rally in the battered AI trade, while Federal Reserve tightening bets lifted Treasury yields and the dollar. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan climbed 4.6 per cent, bouncing back from an eight-month low and heading for its biggest single-day gain in two weeks. Japan's Nikkei added 4.5 per cent as traders returned from a local holiday. South Korea's KOSPI surged 7.5 per cent, while Taiwanese shares jumped 9.1 per cent. Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry's massive buildout. Shares of Nvidia surged 31.5 per cent on Monday, marking their biggest daily percentage gain in 23 years and restoring nearly $1 trillion in value to the company. Companies across the AI industry also rallied sharply, with the Nasdaq 100, which is concentrated in megacap tech companies, jumping more than 6 per cent. "The return of the most important man in the AI industry to the helm of its most important company has eased fear and uncertainty about the AI trade, at least at the margins," despite lingering concerns about slowing AI investment and moderating earnings growth, said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. There are other risks for the market as well, such as uncertainty over US interest rate policy, with investors set to focus on Wednesday's PCE Index data ahead of the Fed's final meeting of 2026, he added. S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq futures edged down 0.2 per cent early on Tuesday. The cash S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indexes surged 4.7 per cent and 6.5 per cent, respectively. AI REBOUND LIFTS FED TIGHTENING BETS The sharp AI rebound has also eased growth concerns and loosened financial conditions, reviving market bets for near-term Fed tightening and lifting front-end Treasury yields and the dollar. Fed funds futures traders are now pricing in a hike at the Fed's December meeting as a certainty, compared with 89 per cent odds on Friday, when stocks tumbled, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The market-implied chance of a supersized 50-basis-point increase in around 5 per cent. The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose for a second day and was last at 4.94 per cent, and the yield on the 2-year note rose to 4.69 per cent. The dollar, meanwhile, hovered near a more than 19-month high against the euro. In commodities, oil prices fell more than 3 per cent to near a three-month low on rising supplies from the Middle East, which offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region. Brent crude futures were flat at $89.50 a barrel after settling down 3.5 per cent at $89.37 a barrel on Monday. Bullion recovered from a more than one-year low, with spot gold last up 0.7 per cent at $3,657.97 per ounce as investors bought the dip.

data.title: Japan's factory activity expands in November, PMI shows
data.description: TOKYO, Nov 24 : Japan's manufacturing activity grew at a slightly faster in November as output and export orders picked up on semiconductor and electronics demand, a preliminary business survey showed on Tuesday. • The S&P Global Flash Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 53.7 in November from 53.3 in October, a preliminary survey by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction. • A key sub-index for factory output grew and new orders rose at a solid pace helped by a sharp rise in export orders. • New export orders accelerated from October thanks to robust demand, especially from other major Asian economies. This lifted new export business at the overall private sector at the fastest rate since January 2018. • Manufacturers were more optimistic than service providers about the business outlook, but confidence in both sectors weakened from October on worries about rising costs, labour shortages and concerns over a slowdown in consumer spending. • Price pressures remained strong across the private sector even as they eased. Input cost inflation slowed to an eight-month low, while output charge inflation weakened to its lowest since March, though both stayed historically sharp. • "Japan's private sector continued to expand midway through the final quarter of the year, but momentum was lost amid a slowdown in service sector activity," said Annabel Fiddes, Economics Associate Director at S&P Global Market Intelligence. • "Uncertainty remains elevated as firms grapple with sharply rising costs and worries over a sustained slowdown in consumer spending." • The services sector weakened, with the flash Japan services PMI slipping to 50.5 from 51.7. • The composite PMI, which combines manufacturing and services, eased to 51.5, a six-month low, from 52.1 in October.

data.title: Social media companies not liable for Buffalo mass shooting, New York's highest court rules
data.description: NEW YORK, Nov 23 : Several major social media companies should not be held liable over accusations that they helped an avowed white supremacist who in 2022 killed 10 Black people at a grocery store in Buffalo, New York, the state's highest court ruled on Monday.  In a 4-3 decision, New York's Court of Appeals let stand a divided lower court ruling that found Alphabet's Google and YouTube, Meta Platforms' Instagram, Reddit and Snap's Snapchat were immune under a federal law that protects online platforms from liability over user content. Monday's majority said victims of Payton Gendron's attack on May 14, 2022, at Tops Friendly Markets failed to show that his actions were a "natural and foreseeable consequence" of the defendants' decisions about how to design and run their platforms. "The shooter’s actions were so extraordinary as to sever the causal chain as a matter of law," the majority said in an unsigned opinion. Gendron was 18 years old at the time of the attack. Many courts have addressed the degree to which Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act should shield social media companies over conduct by young children and teenagers who use their platforms. Matthew Bergman, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, in a statement said his clients are evaluating their legal options. "The families affected by the tragic May 2022 Buffalo grocery store attack deserve accountability when dangerous product design choices contribute to real-world harm," Bergman said. Google, Meta, Reddit and Snap did not immediately respond to requests for comment. SHUTTING THE COURTHOUSE DOOR Victims' relatives, as well as store employees and customers who saw the attack, contended that the defendants' platforms were designed to addict and radicalize users like Gendron.  Dissenting from Monday's decision, Judge Jenny Rivera said juries should decide whether the prevalence of mass shootings would put social media companies on notice that their allegedly defective products, and failure to warn about their dangers, could trigger such violence.  "No federal or state law requires that we slam the courthouse door on plaintiffs’ claims," Rivera wrote. The Court of Appeals also upheld the dismissal of claims against Amazon.com, Discord, 4chan and Twitch Interactive related to Gendron's attack. Lawyers for those companies declined to comment or were not immediately available for comment.  Gendron was sentenced in February 2023 to life in prison without parole, after pleading guilty to state charges including murder and terrorism motivated by hate. He could face the death penalty at a related federal trial, where jury selection began on October 13.

data.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster
data.description: Nov 23 : Anthropic said on Monday it has launched Claude Ship to help developers ship code faster by reviewing changes, fixing problems and deciding which ones can be added to the main code based on rules set by a team. Here are more details: • Claude Ship has three parts: Code Review, which is already available, and two new tools in beta testing: PR Steward and Claude Approvals • Code Review checks proposed code changes and flags problems • PR Steward helps resolve failed automated checks on a code change, conflicts between code changes and reviewer comments • The tool, which is designed to assist developers and not to approve or merge code changes on its own, explains the changes it makes and how to undo them • Claude Approvals can approve routine changes on its own if team rules allow, and send riskier ones to a human • Claude Ship is available from Monday on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for projects on GitHub

data.title: US files action to recover over $1 billion in cryptocurrency stolen in Binance hack
data.description: Nov 23 : The US Justice Department said on Monday that it had filed a civil claim to recover more than $1 billion in cryptocurrency assets stolen by North Korean cyber actors in a recent hack of Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency platform.

data.title: CFTC staff advisory says crypto can count toward reserves, not liquidity rule
data.description: Nov 23 : Some cryptocurrency assets can count toward the reserves that trading platforms and clearinghouses must keep on hand, but not toward a separate liquidity requirement, staff at the US commodities regulator said in an advisory on Monday. Here are the details:  • Staff in the Commodity Futures Trading Commission's Division of Market Oversight and Division of Clearing and Risk issued the advisory. • It applies to swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations. • The advisory addresses three CFTC regulations that require these entities to hold enough financial resources to cover at least 12 months of operating costs. • The staff said bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins may count toward that requirement "subject to appropriate haircuts." • Crypto assets cannot satisfy the separate liquidity requirement because they don't qualify as cash or highly liquid securities under accounting rules, according to the advisory. • CFTC said the advisory only reflects the views of staff and does not create new rules or enforceable rights, is not a no-action position, and does not necessarily represent the views of the commission.

data.title: StarHub confirms merger with M1
data.description: SINGAPORE: StarHub and M1 will combine in an all-share transaction, the telco and M1 parent Keppel confirmed on Tuesday (Nov 24). The deal will unlock estimated operating expenditure synergies with a net present value of S$1.1 billion, the companies said in a media release. StarHub and Keppel earlier confirmed on Sep 23 that they were in talks over a potential deal, months after a proposed acquisition of M1 by rival Simba fell through . Both companies requested a trading halt ahead of the announcement on Tuesday morning. The proposed merger is subject to regulatory approval from Singapore’s Infocomm Media Development Authority and Ministry of Digital Development and Information, shareholder approval of StarHub and Keppel at separate extraordinary general meetings, as well as other applicable transaction conditions, read the media release. Subject to these approvals and conditions, the Proposed Merger is expected to complete by the first half of 2027. Analysts have said that a merger between StarHub and M1 could create an entity large enough to rival market leader Singtel, but may also ease pricing pressures that benefit consumers. This is a developing story . Refresh for updates.

data.title: CFTC finalises permanent data-reporting rules for event contracts
data.description: Nov 23 : The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission finalized permanent data-reporting rules for certain event contracts on Monday, aiming to strengthen oversight of prediction markets. • The rule comes as prediction markets face growing regulatory scrutiny in the US, with questions over federal oversight and market integrity • The final rule creates an alternative reporting framework for certain fully collateralised event contracts that have operated under CFTC staff no-action relief since 2017 • "The CFTC will no longer regulate market participants through a patchwork of no-action letters, which serve as band-aids for unworkable regulations. This final rule is an important step in future-proofing the regulatory framework for event contracts," Chairman Michael Selig said • Under the new framework, reporting markets, futures commission merchants, clearing members and foreign brokers will report data under Parts 15-18 of CFTC regulations, instead of relying on reporting provisions spread across Parts 38, 39, 43 and 45 • The move follows other efforts by the regulator to strengthen federal oversight of prediction markets, including an earlier proposal to classify certain event contracts as swaps

data.title: Meta pauses Class C share issuance amid shareholder lawsuit
data.description: Nov 23 : Meta Platforms said on Monday it will not issue its planned Class C shares while it faces shareholder litigation challenging the company's proposed recapitalization, delaying a share sale program intended to help fund its artificial intelligence investments. • The social media giant agreed not to issue the shares during the pre-trial and trial proceedings in the lawsuit brought by shareholders in Delaware's Court of Chancery. The trial is scheduled to begin on April 19, 2027 • The shareholder litigation challenges Meta's plan to create a new class of non-voting Class C common stock in January 2027 • The structure would effectively result in a two-for-one split and is designed to give Meta flexibility to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting control • The delay also affects Meta's planned $60 billion at-the-market stock sale program, which is not expected to begin until the Class C shares start trading • The company has been investing heavily in advanced chips and data centers as it steps up competition with AI leaders OpenAI and Anthropic, while positioning itself at the forefront of the emerging consumer AI agent race

data.title: Wall Street jumps back as Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO
data.description: NEW YORK: US stocks surged on Monday (Nov 23), led by a big jump in the Nasdaq as Nvidia 's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares after last week's rout. Nvidia's shares shot up as much as 36.6 per cent after the board returned Huang . He had resigned from the company on Nov 12 after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump said he secured a deal with Nvidia 's board to bring back Huang as CEO. Nvidia is widely seen as a cornerstone of the AI trade. The news helped Wall Street recover from last week's sharp selloff. On Friday, the S&P 500 and the Dow both confirmed corrections as worries mounted about the AI trade. The Nasdaq-100 add ed more than US$2 trillion in market value on Monday , while the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 had their biggest daily gains since the market surged after Trump paused his "Liberation Day" tariff package in April 2025. "The thought had been, and it's being borne out today, that Jensen Huang is uniquely important to Nvidia and to the AI trade," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at Globalt Investments. Still, he said, "you have one issue that is resolved - and it's a biggie - but you still have to see how the rest of things play out." The S&P gained 326.78 points, or 4.73 per cent, to end at 7,237.17 points while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1,471.83 points, or 6.51 per cent, to 24,089.56. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose  1,447.98 points, or 3.01 per cent, to 49,595.31. Before Monday, the Nasdaq had come close to entering a bear market as investors worried about the heavy borrowing underpinning AI investment and questioned whether the sector could deliver sufficient returns. Fears of political scrutiny also mounted after Democrats swept the US midterm elections. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index and S&P 500 information technology sector both were sharply higher on Monday, along with megacap stocks such as Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet . Also climbing were neocloud and data-center companies, which had come under sharp selling pressure following Huang's abrupt exit. Other sectors also rose, with energy being the only group in negative territory. "We don't think the rebound has run its course, and at these levels, it's not too late to gradually add back technology exposure," said Andrew Slimmon, senior portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Investment Management. Ahead this week is Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures report, which could give clues about the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook.

data.title: Amazon’s AWS CEO says engineering, not kill switches, is path to AI safety
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 23 : The path to safer AI is not a “kill switch,” it’s building a better mousetrap. That’s the message from Amazon’s AWS CEO Matt Garman in a 1,300-word blog post published on Monday, as fears over rogue agents continue to roil the industry. “We’ve learned that trust isn’t built by making promises about our intentions,” wrote Garman. “It’s built by engineering systems so that outcomes are controlled regardless of what’s running inside them. That principle applies directly to AI.” Even as Anthropic held a record-setting IPO this month, concerns around AI safety and its social impact remain at the forefront. Voters overwhelmingly rejected the aggressive buildout of data centers and pushed back on politicians who promised accelerated AI deployment. Earlier this year, a slew of researchers warned that the pace of AI development poses an existential threat to humanity amid reports that swarms of AI agents colluding together were able to breach computer systems and evade built-in safeguards. Amazon had previously called for more rigorous AI testing and said AI labs should only release models when they are safe.  "No one relies on the emergency brake as their main source of protection on the road," said Garman. "The primary brakes, steering, suspension, and navigation are engineered to work together and keep you safe on every drive, and the emergency brake is there as a last resort. AI systems should be engineered the same way." Garman, who oversees much of Amazon’s AI development and infrastructure like data centers, warned that “hype” around AI safety can distract leaders from the task of building better software that acts responsibly. He said that might include halting production of new models, even though others release them without proper testing or with poor safeguards.  “At most, an agent should inherit the permissions of the human operating it, and in many cases it should have significantly more constrained permissions than that human,” Garman wrote in the blog post. Garman also called for developers to stress test the controls they put on their AI models, noting that the software sometimes acts in unexpected ways. He said labs should also continuously monitor their models and take steps to prevent them from acting outside established boundaries. “The organizations that lead with AI won’t be the ones that are just using the best models,” said Garman.  “They’ll be the ones that also invest in the best engineering discipline around them.”

data.title: Nvidia bears face $12.2 billion hit on Huang's surprise return
data.description: Nov 23 : Nvidia short sellers were staring at about $12.2 billion in paper losses on Monday, their biggest one-day hit since at least 2019, according to ORTEX, after the chipmaker's shares soared on Jensen Huang's surprise return as CEO. The losses, calculated at a share price of $168.50, would erase more than $10.5 billion in paper gains from last week. Short sellers, however, remain up about $14 billion since October 29, ORTEX said. The chip giant shares were last up 33 per cent at $167.14 after Huang was reinstated less than two weeks after resigning over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump had called for his return. Short sellers "are still well ahead since late October, so this hurts but it hasn't undone the trade," said Peter Hillerberg, co-Founder of ORTEX. "Some will be covering, but with only just over 1 per cent of the float short, this looks like a reaction to the news rather than a squeeze."

data.title: Commentary: This is the problem with the circular AI economy
data.description: NEW YORK: Why isn’t circular financing illegal? The question was posed by an anxious CEO at a recent business dinner I attended in California, off the back of a conversation we were having (predictably) about the fallout of Nvidia. The chipmaker has propped up a big chunk of the larger AI ecosystem via loans and equity stakes in customers that buy its products, aka “circular financing”. This creates a market but also layers of interconnected fragility that can ricochet more broadly if things go wrong. It can also make it difficult to differentiate real demand from the speculative kind - hence the anxious question. Nvidia’s earnings report last week was more robust than one might have expected given the turmoil at the company. Still, there is legitimate concern about whether a decline in chip orders over the next few months could mean less vendor financing, and thus a collapse in the larger AI ecosystem. That is in part because the size of this “great AI circular financing circus”, as a recent MacroStrategy report put it, is unprecedented."THE GREAT AI CIRCULAR FINANCING CIRCUS" Nvidia increased its vendor financing by a whopping 1,600 per cent over the past three years, to a total of just under US$700 billion. To compare, Cisco - which lent to dotcom companies to buy routers, switches and other hardware to build out networks in advance of the dotcom collapse - had US$1.3 billion in financed leased debt exposure in March 2001. As in today’s AI bubble, many of those dotcom companies were ordering more equipment than they needed immediately, piling in as the market was growing so quickly. When the boom turned to bust, they were unable to repay Cisco, which in turn had to cut back on loans, creating a feedback loop that eventually led to a sharp decline in orders by 2001. It also helped push the wider market into an earnings recession. The worry now is that while Nvidia was, like Cisco, lending directly to clients, it was also taking equity stakes in customers’ businesses and offering commitments to purchase customer cloud services. What will happen to that funding when sales to China go away, and the company is under incredible political scrutiny? Will all of this cause the off-balance sheet funding bubble to burst, taking down the AI market (on which about half the value of the S&P 500 is directly or indirectly dependent) with it? And if it does, what broader impact might that have on the real economy? A LOOK AT HISTORY OF VENDOR FINANCING To answer that question, it is helpful to think about the history of vendor financing. Supporting customer demand has long been a way for companies at the centre of a boom - particularly a new and transformative infrastructure boom - to create a market for their products. The question for investors is how much of the demand is real versus speculative, to what extent the speculation spills into the banking system, and how much of the vendor investment eventually turns into productive capacity - and over what time.Consider the 19th-century railroad boom, during which rail owners extended credit to farmers to buy land, with the promise that their crops would need to be shipped over those new lines, creating more demand for the railways themselves. Some of those schemes resulted in overleveraged farmers who had to abandon land during crop failures. But research shows that despite the isolated booms and busts off the back of vendor financing, if railroads hadn’t existed in 1890, agricultural land values in the US would have been over 60 per cent lower. Farmers eventually benefited from the development of the rails, as did the economy - but the timeline was decades, not quarters or even years. Vendor financing tends to amplify boom and bust cycles, but it rarely causes full-blown financial crises. The railroad panic of 1873, for example, was about a bond and banking crunch - not railroad lending to farmers. Likewise, the vendor lending by GE Capital, the finance unit of General Electric, to industrial customers in the run-up to the 2008 crisis, or the financing of General Motors dealers by GMAC during the same period, didn’t help the financial panic of the time, but also didn’t fundamentally cause it. Bank exposure to exploding mortgages did that. LESSONS TO BE LEARNED So, what lessons should we take from all this about Nvidia and its potential repercussions? First, it’s likely we haven’t seen the last of the market fallout. Given the magnitude of financing the company was doing, it’s likely that many of the smaller companies in its orbit could take a hit if there is a big lending pullback. If the broader ecosystem falters, that could slow data centre build-out (as could politics), which would have a wider real economy effect. It could be that some hedge funds and private equity shops backing AI will suffer, too. But it’s harder to imagine that the largest financial institutions would go down, given that they’ve been more risk-averse since 2008. It is also possible to imagine that even if none of the companies in question exist in 10 or 20 years, the AI ecosystem will - and we will be wealthier for it. Nervous investors should remember this as they weather the volatility of the next few quarters (or years).

data.title: Trump tells CNBC he was represented at Nvidia board, spoke to Huang
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 23 : US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday said he believed his intervention with Nvidia was "very important," adding he spoke to now reinstated CEO Jensen Huang Sunday night and had been represented at the board meeting.

data.title: Mercury spacecraft BepiColombo 'on track' despite glitch, ESA says
data.description: Nov 23 : The European Space Agency said on Monday the BepiColombo European-Japanese mission to explore Mercury is "on track" and the spacecraft is safe despite a glitch that occurred when it began orbiting the solar system's smallest and innermost planet. ESA confirmed on Saturday that BepiColombo had entered orbit above Mercury after an eight-year journey from Earth, but then disclosed on Sunday that the thrusters used to position the spacecraft properly above the planet had fired for a shorter amount of time than planned. In a statement on Monday, the space agency said that "BepiColombo is safe and in a stable orbit around Mercury." The robotic spacecraft is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter. They have different scientific objectives and are due to separate in the coming weeks. In its statement on Monday, ESA said the mission is "on track for the separation of its two science orbiters" on December 9 as previously planned.  The agency said teams at its European Space Operations Centre worked with lead spacecraft manufacturer Airbus and others to investigate the thruster issue, which "has been traced to a software glitch." ESA said that as BepiColombo passed 395 miles (635 km) above Mercury's surface, its thrusters began firing as planned.  This burn was expected to last 37 minutes, slowing the spacecraft enough to secure its orbit, but the maneuver instead was "autonomously interrupted and the spacecraft had entered safe mode, a protective state designed to keep the spacecraft safe by ceasing all non-essential activities when it encounters unexpected conditions," ESA said. ESA said mission control determined that because the burn had ended prematurely, the spacecraft achieved around 77 per cent of the total planned velocity change. ESA said more thruster burns are scheduled for the months ahead to modify BepiColombo's orbit. ESA has said routine science operations are slated to commence in April. The mission control team is located in Darmstadt, Germany. Mercury, only slightly larger than Earth's moon, is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the planet and just the second to orbit it. The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface. BepiColombo was launched in 2018.
